verses.commentary: Surely the day is coming. It will burn like a furnace. The arrogant and evildoers become stubble. The coming day sets them on fire. Not a root or branch remains. Total combustion. What seemed permanent proves temporary.

But for you who revere my name, the sun of righteousness rises with healing in its rays. You will go out and frolic like well fed calves. Joy and freedom replace fear and bondage. Healing accompanies judgment. The same day destroys and delivers.
You will trample the wicked. They will be ashes under your feet on the day when I act. Role reversal. Those who oppressed become a path. Vindication complete. Power relations inverted.
Remember the law of my servant Moses. The decrees and laws given at Horeb for all Israel. The Old Testament concludes by pointing back to its beginning. Torah remains authoritative. Moses endures.

See, I will send the prophet Elijah before that great and dreadful day of the Lord. Elijah's return announced. John the Baptist comes in Elijah's spirit and power (Luke 1:17). Jesus identifies John as the fulfillment (Matthew 11:14).

He will turn the hearts of parents to children, children to parents. Or else I will come and strike the land with total destruction (cherem, the ban). The Old Testament ends with conditional threat. Reconciliation between generations or utter devastation. The choice stands open. Four hundred years of silence follow, then a voice in the wilderness prepares the way.
